data.hypothesis: Prior scalar unroll choices were all slower than the 55.00 µs baseline, and the staged two-group variant failed correctness on Lena. This contrasting two-group schedule tests whether interleaved lookups followed by one combined validity branch and an all-or-nothing exact-size output commit can reduce valid-path control overhead while keeping invalid input and padding in the existing scalar path. No speedup or correctness result is assumed before controller evaluation.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use the measured outcomes to calibrate expectations for scalar unroll factors; these results do not establish that another schedule cannot help.
memory_lessons.claim: Measured scalar schedules were slower than the 55.00 µs baseline: two groups at 82.32 µs, three at 147.64 µs, four at 63.81 µs, and eight at 81.30 µs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the combined-check two-group candidate to baseline under the official native timing protocol.

memory_lessons.applicability: The fallback path must retain the original input/output position whenever an unrolled group cannot be committed.
memory_lessons.claim: A staged two-group candidate failed a protected correctness check on the 141020-character Lena input, despite passing the smaller visible cases.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check correctness across short inputs, group boundaries, padding cases, random valid inputs, and Lena before timing.

data.notes: The catalog reports five distinct prior programs; its best T3 result is the four-group schedule at 63.81 µs, still above the baseline mean of 55.00 µs. The earlier staged two-group candidate (97ae5147d9be401e) was incorrect on the official Lena case. This candidate instead commits neither group unless both validate. No tests or timings were run here; correctness and performance remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Changed only the bulk decode loop in src/candidate.cpp to interleave scalar table lookups for two independent eight-character groups.
Combined validity checks for both groups before storing output or advancing input, leaving an invalid group for the original scalar fallback.
Kept the existing 21-character guard, exact six-byte-per-group writes, scalar tail and padding handling, and threads behavior; added no explicit SIMD or parallel execution.
